units.zh: 《易》曰：「亢之爲言也，知進而不知退，知存而不知亡。
units.en: The Changes says: "Excess" means knowing when to advance but not when to retreat, knowing how to preserve but not how to perish.
units.literal: The Changes says: "Excess means knowing advance but not retreat, knowing preservation but not loss.

units.zh: 知進退存亡而不失其正者，其唯聖人乎！」
units.en: Only the sage knows advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean!"
units.literal: Knowing advance, retreat, preservation, and loss without losing the Mean—surely only the sage can do this!"

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「知足不辱，知止不殆。」
units.en: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."
units.literal: The Tradition says: "Knowing sufficiency brings no disgrace; knowing when to stop brings no danger."

units.zh: 然則不知夫進退，不達乎止足，殆辱之累，期月而至矣。
units.en: Yet those who misjudge advance and retreat and never grasp sufficiency and stopping invite disgrace and danger within a month.
units.literal: Yet if one does not understand advance and retreat, and does not grasp sufficiency and stopping, the burden of disgrace and danger arrives within a month.

units.zh: 古人之進也，以康世濟務也，以弘道厲俗也。
units.en: Men of old advanced to comfort the age, aid affairs, spread the Way, and sharpen custom.
units.literal: When men of old advanced, it was to bring peace to the age and aid affairs, to spread the Way and sharpen custom.

units.zh: 然其進也，光寵夷易，故愚夫之所乾沒；
units.en: Advance brought easy glory and favor, so fools scrambled for them;
units.literal: When they advanced, glory and favor came easily, so fools scrambled for them;

units.zh: 其退也，苦節艱貞，故庸曹之所忌憚。
units.en: withdrawal meant bitter integrity and hard constancy that vulgar men feared and resented.
units.literal: when they withdrew, bitter integrity and hard constancy made vulgar men fear and resent them.

units.zh: 雖禍敗危亡，陳乎耳目，而輕舉高蹈，寡乎前史。
units.en: Though disaster and ruin lay before their eyes, few in earlier histories lightly rose and walked away.
units.literal: Though disaster, defeat, peril, and ruin lay before their eyes, lightly to rise and walk high—few in earlier histories did so.

units.zh: 漢世張良功成身退，病臥卻粒，比於樂毅、范蠡至乎顛狽，斯爲優矣。
units.en: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, even to their ruin, he was the better case.
units.literal: In Han, Zhang Liang achieved merit and withdrew his person, took to his bed and ceased grain—compared with Yue Yi and Fan Li, down to their ruin, he was the better case.

units.zh: 其後薛廣德及二疏等，去就以禮，有可稱焉。
units.en: Later Xue Guangde and the two Shus withdrew according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.
units.literal: Afterward Xue Guangde and the two Shus and others withdrew and took office according to ritual—there is something to praise in that.

units.zh: 魚豢《魏略·知足傳》，方田、徐於管、胡，則其道本異。
units.en: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.
units.literal: Yu Huan's "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" in the Wei Summary pairs Tian and Xu with Guan and Hu—their Ways were fundamentally different.

units.zh: 謝靈運《晉書·止足傳》，先論晉世文士之避亂者，殆非其人；
units.en: Xie Lingyun's Jin History "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" discusses literary men fleeing disorder—hardly the right men;
units.literal: Xie Lingyun's "Biography of Knowing When to Stop" in the Jin History first discusses Jin-era literary men who fled disorder—hardly the right men;

units.zh: 唯阮思曠遺榮好遁，遠殆辱矣。
units.en: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.
units.literal: only Ruan Sixiao left glory and loved withdrawal, far from nearly suffering disgrace.

units.zh: 《宋書·止足傳》有羊欣、王微，咸其流亞。
units.en: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.
units.literal: The Song History "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" has Yang Xin and Wang Wei—both of that stream.

units.zh: 齊時沛國劉瓛，字子珪，辭祿懷道，棲遲養志，不戚戚於貧賤，不耽耽於富貴，儒行之高者也。
units.en: In Qi, Liu Huan of Pei, styled Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered to nourish his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.
units.literal: In Qi times Liu Huan of Pei, courtesy name Zigui, declined salary and cherished the Way, lingered and nourished his will—neither fretful in poverty nor greedy in wealth: a Confucian of the highest conduct.

units.zh: 梁有天下，小人道消，賢士大夫相招在位，其量力守志，則當世罔聞，時或有致事告老，或有寡志少欲，國史書之，亦以爲《止足傳》云。
units.en: When Liang possessed the realm, petty ways faded and worthy men took office together. Those who measured strength and kept resolve went unmentioned; some reported illness and retired, some had few desires—the state history records them in this Biography of Knowing Sufficiency as well.
units.literal: When Liang possessed the realm, the way of petty men faded; worthy scholar-officials summoned one another to office. Those who measured their strength and kept their resolve went unmentioned in their day; sometimes men reported illness and retired, or had few desires— the state history records them in this "Biography of Knowing Sufficiency" as well.

units.zh: 顧憲之
units.en: Gu Xianzhi
units.literal: Gu Xianzhi

units.zh: 顧憲之字士思，吳郡吳人也。
units.en: Gu Xianzhi, styled Sisi, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Gu Xianzhi, courtesy name Sisi, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 祖抃之，宋鎮軍將軍、湘州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song General Who Pacifies the Army and inspector of Xiangzhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Bianzhi was Song General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 憲之未弱冠，州辟議曹從事，舉秀才，累遷太子舍人、尚書比部郎、撫軍主簿。
units.en: Before he capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; recommended as Flourishing Talent (xiucai), he rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.
units.literal: Before Xianzhi had capped his years, the province appointed him Retainer of the Council; he was recommended as Filial-and-Incorrupt and rose through Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section to Registrar of the Pacification Army.

units.zh: 元徽中，爲建康令。
units.en: In the Yuanhui era he was magistrate of Jiankang.
units.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was Magistrate of Jiankang.

units.zh: 時有盜牛者，被主所認，盜者亦稱己牛，二家辭證等，前後令莫能決。
units.en: A cattle thief was identified by the owner; the thief also claimed the ox was his—both argued equally, and successive magistrates could not decide.
units.literal: At the time there was a cattle thief whom the owner identified; the thief also claimed the ox was his—both households argued with equal force, and successive magistrates could not decide.

units.zh: 憲之至，覆其狀，謂二家曰：「無爲多言，吾得之矣。」
units.en: When Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case and told both households: "Say no more—I have got it."
units.literal: When Xianzhi arrived, he reviewed the case and told both households: "Say no more—I have got it."

units.zh: 乃令解牛，任其所去，牛徑還本主宅，盜者始伏其辜。
units.en: He had the ox untied and let it go where it would; the ox went straight to the true owner's house, and the thief at last confessed.
units.literal: He then had the ox untied and let it go where it would; the ox went straight to the true owner's house, and the thief at last confessed his crime.

units.zh: 發姦擿伏，多如此類，時人號曰神明。
units.en: Exposing wrongdoing and unmasking the hidden—many cases were like this; people called him divine in judgment.
units.literal: Exposing wrongdoing and unmasking the hidden—many cases were like this; people of the time called him divine in judgment.

units.zh: 至於權要請託，長吏貪殘，據法直繩，無所阿縱。
units.en: For powerful men's entreaties and greedy administrators, he held the law straight and never yielded to flattery.
units.literal: As for powerful men's entreaties and long administrators' greed and cruelty, he held the law straight with the cord and never yielded to flattery.

units.zh: 性又清儉，強力爲政，甚得民和。
units.en: Pure and frugal by nature, he governed with firm strength and won the people's harmony.
units.literal: By nature he was also pure and frugal, governing with firm strength, and won the people's harmony exceedingly.

units.zh: 故京師飲酒者得醇旨，輒號爲「顧建康」，言醑清且美焉。
units.en: Hence capital drinkers who got rich flavor called it "Administrator Gu of Jiankang," saying the brew was clear and fine.
units.literal: Hence those who drank in the capital, if they got rich flavor, would call it "Administrator Gu of Jiankang," saying the brew was clear and fine.

units.zh: 遷車騎功曹、晉熙王友。
units.en: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.
units.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Chariots and Cavalry and Friend of the Prince of Jinxi.

units.zh: 齊高帝執政，以爲驃騎錄事參軍，遷太尉西曹掾。
units.en: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.
units.literal: When Qi Gaozu held the government, he made him Recorder of the Rapid Cavalry and transferred him to Western Section Clerk of the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 齊臺建，爲中書侍郎。
units.en: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 齊高帝卽位，除衡陽內史。
units.en: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed administrator of Hengyang.
units.literal: When Qi Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Administrator of Hengyang.

units.zh: 先是，郡境連歲疾疫，死者太半，棺木尤貴，悉裹以葦席，棄之路傍。
units.en: Before this, plague had struck year after year and more than half died; coffin wood was costly, and corpses were wrapped in reed mats and cast beside the road.
units.literal: Before this, within the commandery plague had struck year after year and more than half had died; coffin wood was especially costly, and corpses were wrapped only in reed mats and cast beside the road.

units.zh: 憲之下車，分告屬縣，求其親黨，悉令殯葬。
units.en: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.
units.literal: When Xianzhi took office, he sent word to the subordinate counties to seek kin and had them all buried properly.

units.zh: 其家人絕滅者，憲之爲出公祿，使綱紀營護之。
units.en: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had clerks arrange care.
units.literal: For families whose line was extinguished, Xianzhi paid from public salary and had the clerks arrange care.

units.zh: 又土俗，山民有病，輒云先人爲禍，皆開塚剖棺，水洗枯骨，名爲除祟。
units.en: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they said ancestors were the harm, opening tombs and washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."
units.literal: Again, by local custom when mountain folk fell ill they would say the ancestors were the harm, all opening tombs and coffins, washing dry bones—called "removing the curse."

units.zh: 憲之曉喻，爲陳生死之別，事不相由，風俗遂改。
units.en: Xianzhi enlightened them on life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom changed.
units.literal: Xianzhi enlightened them, setting forth the distinction of life and death and that the affairs do not bear on one another—the custom was thus changed.

units.zh: 時刺史王奐新至，唯衡陽獨無訟者，乃歎曰：「顧衡陽之化至矣。
units.en: Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only Hengyang had no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.
units.literal: At the time Inspector Wang Huan had newly arrived; only in Hengyang was there no litigation, and he sighed: "Administrator Gu of Hengyang's transformation has reached the utmost.

units.zh: 若九郡率然，吾將何事！」
units.en: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"
units.literal: If the nine commanderies were all like this, what would I have to do!"

units.zh: 還爲太尉從事中郎。
units.en: He returned as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
units.literal: He returned to serve as Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

units.zh: 出爲東中郎長史、行會稽郡事。
units.en: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and acting administrator of Kuaiji.
units.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Eastern General of the Gentlemen and Acting Administrator of Kuaiji commandery.

units.zh: 山陰人呂文度有寵於齊武帝，於餘姚立邸，頗縱橫。
units.en: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving overbearingly.
units.literal: Lü Wendu of Shanyin had favor with Qi Wudi and established a lodge in Yuyao, behaving quite overbearingly.

units.zh: 憲之至郡，卽表除之。
units.en: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.
units.literal: When Xianzhi reached the commandery, he memorialized at once to remove it.

units.zh: 文度後還葬母，郡縣爭赴弔，憲之不與相聞。
units.en: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.
units.literal: Wendu later returned to bury his mother; commandery and county competed to attend the mourning, but Xianzhi did not acknowledge it.

units.zh: 文度深銜之，卒不能傷也。
units.en: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.
units.literal: Wendu deeply resented this but in the end could not harm him.

units.zh: 遷南中郎巴陵王長史，加建威將軍、行婺州事。
units.en: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and acting governor of Wuzhou.
units.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Prince of Baling in the Southern General of the Gentlemen, with additional title General Who Establishes Might and Acting Governor of Wuzhou.

units.zh: 時司徒、竟陵王於宣城、臨成、定陵三縣界立屯，封山澤數百里，禁民樵采，憲之固陳不可，言甚切直。
units.en: The Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, enclosed mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbade firewood—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt.
units.literal: At the time the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling, established garrisons on the borders of Xuancheng, Lincheng, and Dingling counties, enclosing mountains and marshes for hundreds of li and forbidding the people firewood and gathering—Xianzhi firmly memorialized that this could not be, his words very blunt and direct.

units.zh: 王答之曰：「非君無以聞此德音。」
units.en: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."
units.literal: The Prince replied: "Without you I would not have heard this virtuous word."

units.zh: 卽命無禁。
units.en: He at once ordered no prohibition.
units.literal: He at once ordered no prohibition.

units.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，兼尚書吏部郎中。
units.en: He was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel Section.
units.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director in the Ministry of Personnel Section.

units.zh: 宋世，其祖覬之嘗爲吏部，於庭植嘉樹，謂人曰：「吾爲憲之種耳。」
units.en: In Song times his grandfather Ji had served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and said: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."
units.literal: In Song times his grandfather Ji had once served in the Ministry of Personnel; in the courtyard he planted a fine tree and told people: "I am planting this for Xianzhi."

units.zh: 至是，憲之果爲此職。
units.en: At this time Xianzhi indeed held that office.
units.literal: At this time Xianzhi indeed held that office.

units.zh: 出爲征虜長史、行南兗州事，遭母憂。
units.en: He went out as Chief Clerk of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians and acting governor of Southern Yanzhou, and encountered mourning for his mother.
units.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Acting Governor of Southern Yanzhou, and encountered mourning for his mother.

units.zh: 服闋，建武中，復除給事黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。
units.en: When mourning ended, in Jianwu he was again appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
units.literal: When mourning ended, in the Jianwu era he was again appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

units.zh: 未拜，仍遷太子中庶子，領吳邑中正。
units.en: Before he took the appointment he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Rectifier of Wu district.
units.literal: Before he took the appointment he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Rectifier of Wu district.

units.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、臨川內史；
units.en: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Linchuan;
units.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Linchuan;

units.zh: 未赴，改授輔國將軍、晉陵太守。
units.en: before he went, the appointment was changed to General Who Assists the State and administrator of Jinling.
units.literal: before he went, the appointment was changed to General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 頃之遇疾，陳解還鄉里。
units.en: Shortly afterward he fell ill and petitioned to return to his home village.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he fell ill and petitioned to return to his home village.

units.zh: 永元初，徵爲廷尉，不拜，除豫章太守。
units.en: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was summoned as Minister of Justice but did not accept; he was appointed administrator of Yuzhang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was summoned as Minister of Justice but did not accept; he was appointed Administrator of Yuzhang.

units.zh: 有貞婦萬晞者，少孀居無子，事舅姑尤孝，父母欲奪而嫁之，誓死不許，憲之賜以束帛，表其節義。
units.en: Chaste widow Wan Xi, widowed young without sons, served her parents-in-law with utmost filiality; her parents wished to force remarriage but she swore to die—Xianzhi bestowed silk and memorialized her integrity.
units.literal: There was a chaste widow, Wan Xi, who widowed young without sons and served her parents-in-law with utmost filiality; her parents wished to force her to remarry but she swore she would rather die—Xianzhi bestowed silk and memorialized her integrity.

units.zh: 中興二年，義師平建康，高祖爲揚州牧，徵憲之爲別駕從事史。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, when the righteous army pacified Jiankang, Gaozu was Governor of Yangzhou and summoned Xianzhi as Retainer of the Separate Chariot.

units.zh: 比至，高祖已受禪，憲之風疾漸篤，固求還吳。
units.en: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.
units.literal: By the time he arrived, Gaozu had already received the abdication; Xianzhi's wind ailment grew severe and he firmly asked to return to Wu.

units.zh: 天監二年，就家授太中大夫。
units.en: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjian, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

units.zh: 憲之雖累經宰郡，資無擔石。
units.en: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.
units.literal: Though Xianzhi had repeatedly governed commanderies, his assets did not amount to a dan of grain.

units.zh: 及歸，環堵，不免饑寒。
units.en: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.
units.literal: When he returned, his ring of walls could not keep out hunger and cold.

units.zh: 八年，卒於家，年七十四。
units.en: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.
units.literal: In the eighth year he died at home, aged seventy-four.

units.zh: 臨終爲制，以敕其子曰：
units.en: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:
units.literal: On his deathbed he made regulations and charged his sons, saying:

units.zh: 夫出生入死，理均晝夜。
units.en: Birth and entering death—reason treats them like day and night.
units.literal: Birth and entering death, death and leaving life—reason treats them like day and night.

units.zh: 生旣不知所從來，死亦安識所往。
units.en: While alive one does not know whence one came; in death how can one know whither one goes?
units.literal: While alive one does not know whence one came; in death how can one know whither one goes?

units.zh: 延陵所云「精氣上歸于天，骨肉下歸於地，魂氣則無所不之」，良有以也。
units.en: What Yanling said—"The refined breath returns to Heaven, flesh and bone to earth, and the soul's breath goes everywhere"—has good grounds.
units.literal: What Yanling said—"The refined breath returns to Heaven, flesh and bone return to earth, and the soul's breath goes everywhere"—has good grounds.

units.zh: 雖復茫昧難徵，要若非妄。
units.en: Though obscure and hard to verify, in essentials it is not vain.
units.literal: Though obscure and hard to verify, in essentials it is not vain.

units.zh: 百年之期，迅若馳隙。
units.en: A span of a hundred years is swift as a galloping gap.
units.literal: A span of a hundred years is swift as a galloping gap.

units.zh: 吾今豫爲終制，瞑目之後，念並遵行，勿違吾志也。
units.en: I now prepare these final regulations in advance; after my eyes close, follow them—do not go against my will.
units.literal: I now prepare these final regulations in advance; after my eyes close, think on them and follow them—do not go against my will.

units.zh: 莊周、澹臺，達生者也；
units.en: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming had attained life;
units.literal: Zhuang Zhou and Tantai Mieming were men who had attained life;

units.zh: 王孫、士安，矯俗者也。
units.en: Wang Sun and Shi An corrected vulgar custom.
units.literal: Wang Sun and Shi An were men who had corrected vulgar custom.

units.zh: 吾進不及達，退無所矯。
units.en: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.
units.literal: In advance I do not reach attainment; in withdrawal I have nothing to correct.

units.zh: 常謂中都之制，允理愜情。
units.en: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.
units.literal: I have always held that the mid-dynasty system accords with reason and satisfies feeling.

units.zh: 衣周於身，示不違禮；
units.en: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;
units.literal: Clothing sufficient for the body shows one does not violate ritual;

units.zh: 棺周於衣，足以蔽臭。
units.en: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.
units.literal: a coffin sufficient for the clothing is enough to cover stench.

units.zh: 入棺之物，一無所須。
units.en: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.
units.literal: What goes into the coffin—nothing is needed.

units.zh: 載以輴車，覆以粗布，爲使人勿惡也。
units.en: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.
units.literal: Carry on a bier-cart, cover with coarse cloth—so people will not be disgusted.

units.zh: 漢明帝天子之尊，猶祭以杅水脯糗；
units.en: Emperor Ming of Han, though Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;
units.literal: Emperor Ming of Han, though honored as Son of Heaven, still sacrificed with ladle-water, dried meat, and parched grain;

units.zh: 范史雲烈士之高，亦奠以寒水乾飯。
units.en: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.
units.literal: Fan Shiyun, lofty as a martyr, also offered cold water and dry rice.

units.zh: 況吾卑庸之人，其可不節衷也？
units.en: How much more for a low and mediocre man like me—can he not restrain his feelings?
units.literal: How much more for a man low and mediocre like me—can he not restrain his feelings?

units.zh: 喪易寧戚，自是親親之情；
units.en: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is kin affection;
units.literal: Mourning is easy but dwelling in grief is hard—this is the affection of kin for kin;

units.zh: 禮奢寧儉，差可得由吾意。
units.en: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.
units.literal: ritual extravagant but dwelling in frugality is somewhat attainable according to my will.

units.zh: 不須常施靈筵，可止設香燈，使致哀者有憑耳。
units.en: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so mourners have something to rely on.
units.literal: Do not constantly set out spirit mats; stop at lighting incense lamps, so those who would mourn have something to rely on.

units.zh: 朔望祥忌，可權安小床，暫設幾席，唯下素饌，勿用牲牢。
units.en: On the first and fifteenth and mourning anniversaries, provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.
units.literal: On the first and fifteenth and on mourning anniversaries, one may provisionally set a small couch and briefly place mats and seats, offering only plain food—do not use sacrificial animals.

units.zh: 蒸嘗之祠，貴賤罔替。
units.en: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.
units.literal: Seasonal sacrifices to ancestors—noble and base alike do not omit them.

units.zh: 備物難辦，多致疏怠。
units.en: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.
units.literal: Full provision is hard to prepare and often leads to neglect.

units.zh: 祠先人自有舊典，不可有闕。
units.en: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.
units.literal: Sacrificing to forebears has its old canon—it cannot be wanting.

units.zh: 自吾以下，祠止用蔬食時果，勿同於上世也。
units.en: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, and seasonal fruit—do not be like upper generations.
units.literal: From me downward, sacrifice only with vegetables, grain, seasonal fruit—do not be like the upper generations.

units.zh: 示令子孫，四時不忘其親耳。
units.en: Show sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.
units.literal: Show the sons and grandsons so the four seasons do not forget their kin.

units.zh: 孔子云：「雖菜羹瓜祭，必齊如也。」
units.en: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."
units.literal: Confucius said: "Even with vegetable broth and melon sacrifice, one must be as if present."

units.zh: 本貴誠敬，豈求備物哉？
units.en: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?
units.literal: The root values sincere reverence—how could one seek full provision?

units.zh: 所著詩、賦、銘、贊幷《衡陽郡記》數十篇。
units.en: He authored poems, fu, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of chapters of the Record of Hengyang Commandery.
units.literal: He authored poems, fu, inscriptions, eulogies, and several tens of chapters of the Record of Hengyang Commandery.

units.zh: 陶季直
units.en: Tao Jizhi
units.literal: Tao Jizhi

units.zh: 陶季直，丹陽秣陵人也。
units.en: Tao Jizhi came from Moling in Danyang.
units.literal: Tao Jizhi was a man of Moling in Danyang.

units.zh: 祖愍祖，宋廣州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Minzu was Song inspector of Guangzhou.
units.literal: His grandfather Minzu was Song Inspector of Guangzhou.

units.zh: 父景仁，中散大夫。
units.en: His father Jingren was palace attendant.
units.literal: His father Jingren was Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 季直早慧，愍祖甚愛異之。
units.en: Minzu loved and favored him exceedingly for his early brilliance.
units.literal: Minzu loved and favored him exceedingly for his early brilliance.

units.zh: 愍祖嘗以四函銀列置於前，令諸孫各取，季直時甫四歲，獨不取。
units.en: Minzu once set four boxes of silver before them and had the grandsons each take one; Jizhi was only four and alone did not take.
units.literal: Minzu once set four boxes of silver in a row before them and had the grandsons each take one; Jizhi was then only four and alone did not take.

units.zh: 人問其故，季直曰：「若有賜，當先父伯，不應度及諸孫，是故不取。」
units.en: When asked why, Jizhi said: "If there is a gift, it should go first to fathers and uncles—not to grandsons—therefore I do not take."
units.literal: When asked why, Jizhi said: "If there is a gift, it should go first to fathers and uncles—it should not pass to grandsons—therefore I do not take."

units.zh: 愍祖益奇之。
units.en: Minzu admired him all the more.
units.literal: Minzu admired him all the more.

units.zh: 五歲喪母，哀若成人。
units.en: At five he lost his mother and mourned as if an adult.
units.literal: At five he lost his mother and mourned as if an adult.

units.zh: 初，母未病，令於外染衣；
units.en: Earlier, before his mother fell ill, she had him dye clothes outside;
units.literal: Earlier, before his mother fell ill, she had him dye clothes outside;

units.zh: 卒後，家人始贖，季直抱之號慟，聞者莫不酸感。
units.en: after her death the household at last redeemed them; Jizhi embraced them and wailed—hearers were all moved to sorrow.
units.literal: after her death the household at last redeemed them; Jizhi embraced them and wailed—hearers were all moved to sorrow.

units.zh: 及長，好學，淡於榮利。
units.en: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.
units.literal: When grown he loved learning and was indifferent to glory and profit.

units.zh: 起家桂陽王國侍郎、北中郎鎮西行參軍，並不起，時人號曰「聘君」。
units.en: He began as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people called him "the Invited Gentleman."
units.literal: He began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Guiyang and Army Aide on the Western Campaign of the Northern General of the Gentlemen, and did not take office—people of the time called him "the Invited Gentleman."

units.zh: 父憂服闋，尚書令劉秉領丹陽尹，引爲後軍主簿、領郡功曹。
units.en: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, concurrently administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.
units.literal: When mourning for his father ended, Liu Bing, who was concurrently Administrator of Danyang, appointed him Chief Clerk of the Rear Army and concurrently Commandery Merit Officer.

units.zh: 出爲望蔡令，頃之以病免。
units.en: He went out as magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.
units.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Wangcai; shortly afterward he was excused on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 時劉秉、袁粲以齊高帝權勢日盛，將圖之，秉素重季直，欲與之定策。
units.en: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.
units.literal: At the time Liu Bing and Yuan Can, because Qi Gaozu's power grew daily, were about to plot against him; Bing had always esteemed Jizhi and wished to settle strategy with him.

units.zh: 季直以袁、劉儒者，必致顛殞，固辭不赴。
units.en: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.
units.literal: Jizhi held that Yuan and Liu were Confucians and would surely come to ruin, and firmly declined to go.

units.zh: 俄而秉等伏誅。
units.en: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.
units.literal: Shortly afterward Bing and the others were executed.

units.zh: 齊初，爲尚書比部郎，時褚淵爲尚書令，與季直素善，頻以爲司空司徒主簿，委以府事。
units.en: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; Chu Yuan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar to the Minister of Works and Minister of Education, entrusting him with bureau affairs.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice Comparison Section; at the time Chu Yuan was Minister of Works and was on good terms with Jizhi, repeatedly making him Registrar of the Masters of Works and Minister of Works, entrusting him with bureau affairs.

units.zh: 淵卒，尚書令王儉以淵有至行，欲諡爲文孝公，季直請曰：「文孝是司馬道子諡，恐其人非具美，不如文簡。」
units.en: When Yuan died, Wang Jian wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."
units.literal: When Yuan died, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Jian, because Yuan had utmost conduct, wished to posthumously title him Duke Wenxiao; Jizhi petitioned: "Wenxiao was Sima Daozi's posthumous title—I fear the man was not wholly good; better Wenjian."

units.zh: 儉從之。
units.en: Jian followed this.
units.literal: Jian followed this.

units.zh: 季直又請儉爲淵立碑，終始營護，甚有吏節，時人美之。
units.en: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much official conduct; people praised this.
units.literal: Jizhi also asked Jian to erect a stele for Yuan and saw to it from start to finish—very much the conduct of an official; people of the time praised this.

units.zh: 遷太尉記室參軍。
units.en: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.
units.literal: He was transferred to Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Grand Marshal's office.

units.zh: 出爲冠軍司馬、東莞太守，在郡號爲清和。
units.en: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.
units.literal: He went out as Army Aide to the Champion and Administrator of Dongguan; in the commandery he was known as pure and harmonious.

units.zh: 還除散騎侍郎，領左衛司馬，轉鎮西諮議參軍。
units.en: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.
units.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel of the Left Guard, then transferred to Army Adviser on the Western Campaign.

units.zh: 齊武帝崩，明帝作相，誅鋤異己，季直不能阿意，明帝頗忌之，乃出爲輔國長史、北海太守。
units.en: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent and purged dissenters; Jizhi could not flatter him and Mingdi feared him, sending him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and administrator of Beihai.
units.literal: When Qi Wudi died, Mingdi became regent, executed and purged those unlike himself; Jizhi could not flatter his intent and Mingdi quite feared him, so he sent him out as Chief Clerk Who Assists the State and Administrator of Beihai.

units.zh: 邊職上佐，素士罕爲之者。
units.en: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.
units.literal: Chief aide on a frontier post—plain scholars rarely held it.

units.zh: 或勸季直造門致謝，明帝旣見，便留之，以爲驃騎諮議參軍，兼尚書左丞。
units.en: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and Director of the Left in the Secretariat.
units.literal: Some urged Jizhi to call at his gate and apologize; once Mingdi saw him he kept him, making him Army Adviser on the Rapid Cavalry and concurrently Director of the Left in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 仍遷建安太守，政尚清靜，百姓便之。
units.en: He was then transferred to administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.
units.literal: He was then transferred to Administrator of Jian'an; his government prized quiet purity and the people found it easy.

units.zh: 還爲中書侍郎，遷遊擊將軍、兼廷尉。
units.en: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and minister of justice.
units.literal: On return he was Attendant of the Secretariat and transferred to General Who Strikes the Foe and concurrently Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 梁臺建，遷給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was transferred to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 常稱仕至二千石，始願畢矣，無爲務人間之事，乃辭疾還鄉里。
units.en: He often said that serving to two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned home.
units.literal: He often said that serving to the rank of two-thousand-dan salary fulfilled his original wish, and he would not busy himself with worldly affairs—then he pleaded illness and returned to his home village.

units.zh: 天監初，就家拜太中大夫。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace at his home.

units.zh: 高祖曰：「梁有天下，遂不見此人。」
units.en: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."
units.literal: Gaozu said: "Liang has possessed the realm, yet I never saw this man."

units.zh: 十年，卒於家，時年七十五。
units.en: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.
units.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged seventy-five.

units.zh: 季直素清苦絕倫，又屏居十餘載，及死，家徒四壁，子孫無以殯斂，聞者莫不傷其志焉。
units.en: Jizhi was pure and bitter beyond compare; he lived in seclusion more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—descendants had no means for burial; hearers grieved for his resolve.
units.literal: Jizhi was by nature pure and bitter beyond compare; he also lived in seclusion for more than ten years, and at death his house had only bare walls—sons and grandsons had no means for burial; hearers all grieved for his resolve.

units.zh: 蕭眎素
units.en: Xiao Shisu
units.literal: Xiao Shisu

units.zh: 蕭眎素，蘭陵人也。
units.en: Xiao Shisu came from Lanling.
units.literal: Xiao Shisu was a man of Lanling.

units.zh: 祖思話，宋征西儀同三司；
units.en: His grandfather Sihua was Song General of the West on Equal Terms with the Three Excellencies;
units.literal: His grandfather Sihua was Song General of the West on Equal Terms with the Three Excellencies;

units.zh: 父惠明，吳興太守；
units.en: his father Huiming was administrator of Wuxing;
units.literal: his father Huiming was Administrator of Wuxing;

units.zh: 皆有盛名。
units.en: both had great fame.
units.literal: both had great fame.

units.zh: 眎素早孤貧，爲叔父惠休所收卹。
units.en: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in by his uncle Huixiu.
units.literal: Shisu was orphaned young and poor and was taken in and supported by his uncle Huixiu.

units.zh: 起家爲齊司徒法曹行參軍，遷著作佐郎、太子舍人、尚書三公郎。
units.en: He began as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section.
units.literal: He began his career as Army Aide in the Law Section of the Qi Minister of Works, transferred to Assistant Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Director of the Three Excellencies Section in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 永元末，爲太子洗馬。
units.en: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was Groom of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 梁臺建，高祖引爲中尉驃騎記室參軍。
units.en: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.
units.literal: When the Liang regime was established, Gaozu appointed him Retainer of the Masters of Affairs in the Rapid Cavalry and Central Commandant.

units.zh: 天監初，爲臨川王友，復爲太子中舍人、丹陽尹丞。
units.en: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then Cadet of the Heir Apparent and assistant to the administrator of Danyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Friend of the Prince of Linchuan, then again Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Assistant to the Administrator of Danyang.

units.zh: 初拜，高祖賜錢八萬，眎素一朝散之親友。
units.en: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.
units.literal: On first taking office Gaozu bestowed eighty thousand cash; Shisu in one morning scattered it among kin and friends.

units.zh: 又遷司徒左西屬、南徐州治中。
units.en: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and concurrent administrator of Southern Xuzhou.
units.literal: He was again transferred to Western Section Clerk of the Left in the Minister of Works and Concurrent Administrator of Southern Xuzhou.

units.zh: 性靜退，少嗜欲，好學，能清言，榮利不關於口，喜怒不形於色。
units.en: Quiet and retiring by nature, with few desires; he loved learning, spoke with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.
units.literal: By nature he was quiet and retiring, with few desires; he loved learning, could speak with pure refinement, and profit and glory did not touch his lips—joy and anger did not show on his face.

units.zh: 在人間及居職，並任情通率，不自矜高，天然簡素，士人以此咸敬之。
units.en: Among people and in office he was open and direct, never proud; naturally plain and simple—scholars all honored him for this.
units.literal: Among people and in office he was always according to feeling, open and direct, never proud of himself; naturally plain and simple—scholar-gentry all honored him for this.

units.zh: 及在京口，便有終焉之志，乃於攝山築室。
units.en: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.
units.literal: When at Jingkou he already had the will to end his days there and built a house on Mt She.

units.zh: 會徵爲中書侍郎，遂辭不就，因還山宅，獨居屏事，非親戚不得至其籬門。
units.en: Summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat, he declined; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.
units.literal: He was summoned as Attendant of the Secretariat and then declined and did not go; he returned to his mountain dwelling, lived alone and screened affairs, and kin and friends could not reach his hedge gate.

units.zh: 妻，太尉王儉女，久與別居，遂無子。
units.en: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.
units.literal: His wife was the daughter of Grand Marshal Wang Jian; long separated from him, in the end there were no sons.

units.zh: 八年，卒。
units.en: In the eighth year he died.
units.literal: In the eighth year he died.

units.zh: 親故迹其事行，諡曰貞文先生。
units.en: Kin and friends traced his conduct and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.
units.literal: Kin and friends traced his conduct and deeds and gave the posthumous title Recluse Zhenwen.

units.en: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.
units.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.

units.zh: 史臣曰：顧憲之、陶季直，引年者也，蕭眎素則宦情鮮焉。
units.en: The historian says: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi cited age to withdraw; Xiao Shisu had little taste for office.
units.literal: The historian says: Gu Xianzhi and Tao Jizhi cited age to withdraw; Xiao Shisu had little taste for office.

units.zh: 比夫懷祿耽寵，婆娑人世，則殊間矣。
units.en: Compared with those who hug salary and cling to favor, lingering among men—how utterly different!
units.literal: Compared with those who hug salary and cling to favor, lingering among men—how utterly different!

units.zh: 父天生，宋末爲列將，於石頭克司徒袁粲，以勳至巴西、梓潼二郡太守，上黃縣男。
units.en: His father Tiansheng, a ranked general in late Song, took Shitou and defeated Minister over the Masses Yuan Can; for merit he became administrator of Brazil and Zitong and was made Marquis of Shanghuang district.
units.literal: His father Tiansheng in late Song was a ranked general; at Shitou he defeated Minister over the Masses Yuan Can, and by merit rose to Administrator of the two commanderies Brazil and Zitong, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanghuang district.

units.zh: 時明帝謀入嗣位，朝之舊臣皆引參謀策。
units.en: Mingdi was then plotting to enter the succession; old courtiers were all drawn into counsel.
units.literal: Mingdi was then plotting succession to the throne; old ministers of the court were all drawn into counsel.

units.zh: 明帝下詔曰：「夫超然榮觀，風流自遠；
units.en: Mingdi issued an edict: "To stand beyond glory is to see the world from far off;
units.literal: Mingdi issued an edict: "One who stands apart from glory views the world from afar;

units.zh: 初，齊明帝及覽父綍、東海徐孝嗣，並爲吳興，號稱名守，覽皆欲過之！
units.en: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
units.literal: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!

units.zh: 建武四年，詔徵爲侍中、中書令，遂抗表不應召。
units.en: In Jianwu's fourth year an edict summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director; he memorialized and refused.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director; he submitted a memorial refusing the summons.

units.zh: 蹈彼幽人，英華罕值。
units.en: to walk the hermit's way is to bloom in solitude.
units.literal: one who treads the hermit's path is rarely met in full flower.

units.zh: 故長揖楚相，見稱南國；
units.en: hence the long bow of the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
units.literal: Hence the long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;

units.zh: 高謝漢臣，取貴良史。
units.en: the Han worthy's lofty refusal won honor from fine historians.
units.literal: the Han worthy's high refusal won honor from fine historians.

units.zh: 新除侍中、中書令朏，早藉羽儀，夙標清尚，登朝樹績，出守馳聲。
units.en: The newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director Fei long wore court insignia and from youth bore a clear name; in court he built merit, abroad he made his name heard.
units.literal: The newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director Fei long bore the court insignia and from youth bore a pure reputation; in court he built merit, going out he made his name heard.

units.zh: 遂斂跡康衢，拂衣林沚，抱箕潁之餘芳，甘憔悴而無悶。
units.en: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook dust from forest robes, keeping the after-scent of Jiqian and Ying, glad in lean exile without regret.
units.literal: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook the dust from his forest robes, embracing the lingering fragrance of Jiqian and Ying, content in lean exile without regret.

units.zh: 撫事懷人，載留欽想。
units.en: Hearing his story, one keeps him in honored thought.
units.literal: Hearing of his deeds one keeps him in honored thought.

units.zh: 宜加優禮，用旌素概。
units.en: Let added courtesy mark his plain integrity.
units.literal: He should receive added courtesy to mark his plain integrity.

units.zh: 可賜床帳褥席，俸以卿祿，常出在所。」
units.en: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always sent to his dwelling."
units.literal: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always provided at his dwelling."

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 又求「樂毅有後乎？」
units.en: He also asked: "Does Yue Yi have descendants?"
units.literal: He also asked: "Does Yue Yi have descendants?"

units.zh: 永明九年，雍州刺史王奐反，敕遣僧珍隸平北將軍曹虎西爲典籤，帶新城令。
units.en: In Yongming year nine, Yongzhou inspector Wang Huan rebelled; Sengzhen was sent west under Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu as Master of Documents, with concurrent magistracy of Xincheng.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, Inspector of Yongzhou Wang Huan rebelled; an edict sent Sengzhen under the Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu west as Master of Documents, with concurrent charge of Xincheng.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」
units.en: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"
units.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"

units.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。
units.en: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
units.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

units.zh: 太祖高皇帝篤猶子之愛，降家人之慈；
units.en: Grand Ancestor Gao cherished a nephew as a son and gave the kindness of kin under one roof;
units.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao cherished the love due a nephew-son and granted the kindness shown within a household;

units.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。
units.en: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.
units.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 儉雅欽重昉，以爲當時無輩。
units.en: Jian prized him deeply and said no man of the time matched him.
units.literal: Jian deeply admired Fang and thought there was no equal in the age.

units.zh: 夫種、蠡無一罪，身死亡；
units.en: Wen Zhong and Fan Li had committed no such crimes, yet they still perished.
units.literal: Wen Zhong and Fan Li committed no such crimes, yet they died.

units.zh: 齊高帝受禪，悉誅宋室近屬，將及季連等，太宰褚淵素善之，固請乃免。
units.en: When Qi Gaozu took the throne he meant to kill every near branch of Song; Lijian was next, but Chu Yuan, who had long favored him, pleaded until he was spared.
units.literal: When Qi Gaozu accepted the abdication, he was set to slay all near kin of the Song house; Lijian's turn was coming, but the grand minister Chu Yuan, who had long favored him, pleaded hard and he was spared.

units.zh: 列傳第二十二 羊欣張敷王微
units.en: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei
units.literal: Biography 22: Yang Xin, Zhang Fu, and Wang Wei

units.zh: 王微，字景玄，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘弟子也。
units.en: Wang Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, was from Linyi in Langye and a nephew of Grand Mentor Wang Hong.
units.literal: Wang Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the younger son of the younger brother of Grand Mentor Hong.

units.zh: 微少好學，無不通覽，善屬文，能書畫，兼解音律、醫方、陰陽術數。
units.en: From youth Wei loved learning and read broadly; he wrote well, painted and practiced calligraphy, and knew music, medicine, and the arts of yin-yang and prognostication.
units.literal: From youth Wei loved learning and there was nothing he did not read through; he was skilled at literary composition, could write and paint, and also understood music, medical prescriptions, and yin-yang numerology.

units.zh: 吾實倦遊醫部，頗曉和藥，尤信《本草》，欲其必行，是以躬親，意在取精。
units.en: I have grown weary of medical offices, understand compounding fairly well, and especially trust the Materia Medica; wishing remedies to be effective, I gather herbs myself to obtain the finest.
units.literal: I truly am weary of wandering the medical departments, quite understand compounding drugs, especially trust the Materia Medica, wishing it must be effective—therefore personally attend, intent on taking the refined.

units.zh: 太祖以其善筮，賜以名蓍。
units.en: Taizu, because he was skilled at divination, bestowed famous yarrow stalks on him.
units.literal: Taizu because he was skilled at divination bestowed famous yarrow stalks on him.

units.zh: 起家司徒祭酒，轉主簿，始興王濬後軍功曹記室參軍，太子中舍人，始興王友。
units.en: He entered office as Libationer of the Minister of Works, then chief clerk, Merit Officer and Record-House Aide on Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army staff, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household, and Friend to the Prince of Shixing.
units.literal: He began his career as Libationer of the Minister of Works, became chief clerk, Merit Officer and Record-House Staff Aide in Prince of Shixing Jun's Rear Army, Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, and Friend to the Prince of Shixing.

units.zh: 微常住門屋一間，尋書玩古，如此者十餘年。
units.en: Wei lived constantly in a single gate-house room, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—for more than ten years.
units.literal: Wei constantly dwelt in one room of the gate house, seeking books and enjoying antiquities—thus for more than ten years.

units.zh: 父孺，光祿大夫。
units.en: His father Ru was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: His father Ru was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 弟僧謙，亦有才譽，為太子舍人，遇疾，微躬自處治，而僧謙服藥失度，遂卒。
units.en: His younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation and served as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household; when he fell ill Wei treated him personally, but Sengqian took medicine in excess and died.
units.literal: Younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation, served as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household; encountering illness, Wei personally attended treatment, yet Sengqian took medicine beyond measure and thus died.

units.zh: 微因此又與從弟僧綽書曰：
units.en: Wei therefore wrote to his younger cousin Sengchuo:
units.literal: Wei therefore also wrote to his younger cousin Sengchuo saying:

units.zh: 且弟曠違兄姊，迄將十載，姊時歸來，終不任輿曳入閣，兄守金城，永不堪扶抱就路，若不憊疾，非性僻而何。
units.en: Your younger brother has been away from his siblings nearly ten years; when my sister visits I cannot endure being carried in a carriage through the gate; my brother holds Jincheng and I can never bear being helped along the road—if this is not illness, what else could it be but a perverse nature?
units.literal: Moreover your younger brother has been absent from elder brother and sisters nearly ten years; when sister returned, I could never bear to be dragged in a carriage into the gate; elder brother guards Jincheng, forever unable to bear being supported on the road—if this is not weariness of illness, what is perverse nature?

units.zh: 成童便往來居舍，晨省復經周旋，加有諸甥，亦何得頓絕慶弔。
units.en: Since childhood I have visited family homes for morning calls and social rounds; with many nephews besides, how can I abruptly cut off congratulations and condolence?
units.literal: From childhood I have gone back and forth to residences; morning calls and again social rounds—with many nephews besides, how can one abruptly cut off congratulations and condolence?

units.zh: 年十六，州舉秀才，衡陽王義季右軍參軍，並不就。
units.en: At sixteen the province nominated him as Cultivated Talent and Prince of Hengyang Yiji made him aide on the Right Army staff—he took neither post.
units.literal: At sixteen the province recommended him as Cultivated Talent; aide to the Right Army under Prince of Hengyang Yiji—he accepted neither.

units.zh: 父憂去官，服闋，除南平王鑠右軍諮議參軍。
units.en: He left office for his father's mourning; when the period ended he was appointed Consultation Aide on Prince of Nanping Shuo's Right Army staff.
units.literal: On his father's death he left office; when mourning was complete he was appointed Consultation Staff Aide to the Right Army under Prince of Nanping Shuo.

units.zh: 微素無宦情，稱疾不就。
units.en: Wei had never sought office and pleaded illness rather than accept.
units.literal: Wei had never had desire for office; he claimed illness and did not accept.

units.zh: 仍除中書侍郎，又擬南琅邪、義興太守，並固辭。
units.en: Appointments followed as Palace Gentleman and as Governor of Southern Langye and Yixing—but he firmly declined them all.
units.literal: He was still removed and made Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat; he was also slated for Governor of Southern Langye and Governor of Yixing—he firmly declined all.

units.zh: 吏部尚書江湛舉微為吏部郎，微與湛書曰：
units.en: Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan nominated Wei as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Wei wrote him:
units.literal: Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan recommended Wei as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Wei wrote to Zhan saying:

units.zh: 弟心病亂度，非但蹇蹙而已，此處朝野所共知。
units.en: Your younger brother suffers a disordered heart, not mere lameness—that is known to court and countryside alike.
units.literal: Your younger brother's heart illness is a disorder of confusion, not merely lameness and constriction—this the court and countryside together know.

units.zh: 騶會忽扣蓽門，閭里咸以為祥怪，君多識前世之載，天值何其易傾。
units.en: Outriders suddenly knocked at my humble door; neighbors took it for a portent. You who have read the records of former ages know how easily Heaven's favor can overturn.
units.literal: Outriders suddenly knocked at my humble gate; neighbors all took it for an omen strange or ill—you who have read much of former ages' records, how easily Heaven's appointment can topple!

units.zh: 弟受海內駭笑，不過如燕石禿鶖邪，未知君何以自解於良史邪？
units.en: Your younger brother will become a laughingstock throughout the realm—no better than the stone goose or the bald ibis, perhaps. How will you answer the impartial historian?
units.literal: Your younger brother will receive the empire's startled laughter—no more than goose-stone or a bald osprey, is it not? I do not know how you will explain yourself to the good historian.

units.zh: 今雖王道鴻鬯，或有激朗於天表，必欲探援潛寶，傾海求珠，自可卜肆巫祠之間，馬棧牛口之下，賞劇孟於博徒，拔卜式於芻牧。
units.en: Though the royal way now flourishes, men of brilliance may still appear from on high; if you wish to seek hidden talent and pearls from the deep, you may find them between the fortune-teller's stall and the shaman's shrine, in the stable and the cattle pen—as when Ju Meng was valued among gamblers or Bu Shi was drawn up from the pasture.
units.literal: Though the royal way now flourishes and spreads, there may be those stirred to brilliance above the heavens; if one must probe and draw forth hidden treasures and tilt the sea to seek pearls, one may between diviner's stalls and shaman shrines, beneath horse lodges and ox mouths, reward Ju Meng among gamblers and raise up Bu Shi from cattle tending.

units.zh: 亦有西戎孤臣，東都戒士，上窮範馳之御，下盡詭遇之能，兼鱗雜襲者，必不乏於世矣。
units.en: Western frontier exiles and eastern capital veterans abound—men who master charioteering at one extreme and cunning stratagem at the other; the world is never short of men who combine many talents.
units.literal: There are also isolated subjects of the western borderlands, guardians from the eastern capital, exhausting at the top the driving of Fan and Chi and at the bottom all the skills of crafty encounter; those with both scales mixed and overlapping must certainly not be lacking in the world.

units.zh: 且廬於承明，署乎金馬，皆明察之官，又賢於管庫之末。
units.en: The scholars lodged at Chenming and posted at the Golden Horse Gate are all men of keen judgment—far worthier than a post at the bottom of the granary rolls.
units.literal: Moreover those lodged at Chenming and posted at Golden Horse are all officials of clear scrutiny, again more worthy than the lowest post of keeper of stores.

units.zh: 何為劫勒通家疾病人，塵穢難堪之選，將以靖國，不亦益囂乎？
units.en: Why force upon the state a sick man from a great family, a choice foul and unfit, in the name of good government—would that not only make matters worse?
units.literal: Why forcibly press a man of an allied house who is ill, a choice filthy and unbearable, intending to pacify the state—is it not the more to increase clamor?

units.zh: 《書》云：「任官維賢才」。
units.en: The Documents says, "In appointing officials, set merit and talent first."
units.literal: The Documents says: "In appointing officials, set merit and talent first."

units.zh: 而君擢士先疹廢，芃芃棫樸，似不如此。
units.en: Yet you choose officials by starting with the sick and broken—the ode's thriving saplings were not chosen that way.
units.literal: Yet you promote men beginning with those wasted by rash and illness—the luxuriant elm saplings do not seem to be thus.

units.zh: 比君曰表裏，無假長目飛耳也。
units.en: When you speak of knowing a man inside and out, you need no spies with far-reaching eyes and ears.
units.literal: When you speak of inner and outer, there is no need for long eyes and flying ears.

units.zh: 常謂生遭太公，將即華士之戮；
units.en: I have often said that had I lived in the age of the Grand Duke of Qi, I would soon have shared Hua Shi's fate;
units.literal: I have often said that if born in the age of the Grand Duke, I would soon meet the execution of the Flower Gentleman;

units.zh: 幸遇管叔，必蒙僻儒之養。
units.en: had I met Uncle Guan instead, I would surely have been kept alive as an eccentric scholar.
units.literal: fortunate to meet Uncle Guan, I would surely receive the fostering of an eccentric scholar.

units.zh: 光武以馮衍才浮其實，故棄而不齒。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu found Feng Yan's talent greater than his substance and cast him aside without a place at court.
units.literal: Emperor Guangwu, because Feng Yan's talent floated above his substance, cast him aside and did not rank him among his teeth.

units.zh: 諸葛孔明云：「來敏亂郡，過於孔文舉。」
units.en: Zhuge Liang said, "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder—worse than Kong Rong."
units.literal: Zhuge Kongming said: "Lai Min throws a commandery into disorder, exceeding Kong Wenju."

units.zh: 況無古人之才槩，敢干周、漢之常刑。
units.en: How much less do I possess the capacity of the ancients, yet dare to invite the ordinary penalties of Zhou and Han!
units.literal: How much more when one lacks the capacity of the ancients yet dares to offend against the regular punishments of Zhou and Han!

units.zh: 彼二三英賢，足為曉治與否？
units.en: Do those two or three worthy men suffice to show whether one understands good government?
units.literal: Are those two or three worthy men enough to show understanding of governance or not?

units.zh: 恐君逄此時，或亦不免高閣，乃復假名不知己者，豈欲自比衛賜邪？
units.en: I fear that in such a time you too may not escape disgrace in high office, yet you borrow the name of one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?
units.literal: I fear that when you meet such a time you likewise may not escape the high pavilion; yet you borrow a name from one who does not know you—do you wish to compare yourself to Wei Ci?

units.zh: 君欲高斅山公，而以仲容見處，徒以搥提禮學，本不參選，鄙夫瞻彼，固不任下走，未知新沓何如州陵耳。
units.en: You wish to take Mount Gong as your model yet treat me like Ruan Zhongrong; raised on ritual learning, I was never on the selection rolls—a coarse man like me cannot serve as your runner, and I do not know how the new appointee compares with you, Zhouling.
units.literal: You wish to imitate high Mount Gong, yet treat me as Zhongrong; merely because I was raised on ritual learning I was never in the selection lists—this coarse fellow looking on that naturally cannot serve as a runner; I do not know what the new entrant is like compared with Zhouling.

units.zh: 而作不師古，坐亂官政，誣飾蚯蚓，冀招神龍，如復託以真素者，又不宜居華留名，有害風俗。
units.en: Yet acting without antiquity as your guide you disturb official government, dressing up an earthworm and hoping to summon a dragon; if one truly relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.
units.literal: Yet acting without taking antiquity as teacher you disturb official government, bedecking an earthworm and hoping to summon a divine dragon; if one again relies on plain authenticity, one should not dwell in glory and leave a name—harmful to custom.

units.zh: 君亦不至期人如此，若交以為人賜，舉未以己勞，則商販之事，又連所不忍聞也。
units.en: You should not expect such a man either; if friendship is treated as a gift from others and promotion comes without one's own effort—that is merchant's business, and something I cannot bear to hear.
units.literal: You also should not expect a man so; if association is taken as a gift from others, and promotion without one's own labor—then the affairs of merchants, again something one cannot bear to hear.

units.zh: 豈謂不肖易擢，貪者可誘，凡此數者，君必居一焉。
units.en: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be bought—of all these you must be guilty of at least one.
units.literal: Do you mean that the unworthy are easy to promote and the greedy can be enticed—of all these several you must occupy one.

units.zh: 雖假天口於齊駢，藉鬼說於周季，公孫碎毛髮之文，莊生縱漭瀁之極，終不能舉其契，為之辭矣。
units.en: Though one had the eloquence of the Qi persuaders, the ghost lore of late Zhou, Gongsun Long's hair-splitting disputations, or Zhuangzi's boundless paradoxes, one still could not justify this appointment.
units.literal: Though one borrow Heaven's mouth from the Qi persuader, borrow ghostly discourse from the Zhou season, Gongsun split the essay of hair and down, Zhuangzi let the vast flood to its extreme—still one cannot raise their bond and make excuse for it.

units.zh: 子將明魂，必靈咍於萬里，汝、潁餘彥，將拂衣而不朝。
units.en: Zizhan's bright spirit must laugh in the dark from afar; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their robes and refuse court.
units.literal: Zizhan's bright soul must laugh darkly at ten thousand li; the remaining fine men of Ru and Ying will brush their coats and not attend court.

units.zh: 浮華一開，風俗或從此而爽。
units.en: Once ostentation is unleashed, custom may slip away from this.
units.literal: Once ostentation opens, custom may from this slip away.

units.zh: 鬼谷以揣情為最難，何君忖度之輕謬。
units.en: Guiguzi held gauging a man's heart the hardest art—how lightly and absurdly you judge!
units.literal: Guiguzi held gauging sentiment the hardest—how lightly and absurdly you estimate!

units.zh: 今有此書，非敢叨擬中散，誠不能顧影負心，純盜虛聲，所以綿絡累紙，本不營尚書虎爪板也。
units.en: This letter is not written to imitate Ji Kang; I truly cannot look at my shadow and betray my heart or steal empty fame; these pages are strung together because I never sought the Ministry's appointment tablet.
units.literal: Now having this letter, I do not dare presumptuously to imitate the Master of Dispersal; truly I cannot look at my shadow and betray my heart, purely stealing empty fame; therefore these pages strung together—I never schemed for the Ministry's tiger-claw board.

units.zh: 然生平之意，自於此都盡。
units.en: Yet the purpose of my life ends here entirely.
units.literal: Yet the intent of my lifetime ends here entirely.

units.zh: 君平公云：「生我名者殺我身。」
units.en: Lord Junping said, "He who gives me fame kills my person."
units.literal: Lord Junping said: "He who gives me fame kills my person."

units.zh: 天爵且猶滅名，安用吏部郎哉！
units.en: Heavenly honor already destroys one's name—what use is the post of Director of the Ministry of Personnel!
units.literal: Heavenly ennoblement already extinguishes name—what use is Director of the Ministry of Personnel!

units.zh: 其舉可陋，其事不經，非獨搢紳者不道，僕妾皆將咲之。
units.en: This recommendation is contemptible and the affair irregular; not only will the gentry refuse to speak of it—even servants and concubines will laugh.
units.literal: This recommendation is contemptible, this affair uncanonical; not only will gentry not speak of it—servants and concubines will all laugh.

units.zh: 忽忽不樂，自知壽不得長，且使千載知弟不詐諼耳。
units.en: Restless and unhappy, I know my years will not be long; yet let a thousand years know your younger brother does not lie.
units.literal: Restless and unhappy, I know my years will not be long; yet let a thousand years know your younger brother does not feign falsely.

units.zh: 吾雖無人鑒，要是早知弟，每共宴語，前言何嘗不以止足為貴。
units.en: Though I am no judge of men, I have known you long; whenever we talked at leisure, did we not always prize knowing when to stop?
units.literal: Though I have no mirror of men, I have known you early; whenever we feasted and spoke together, in former words how did we not take knowing when to stop as precious?

units.zh: 且持盈畏滿，自是家門舊風，何為一旦落漠至此，當局苦迷，將不然邪！
units.en: Holding fast when full and fearing excess is our family's old way—why have you fallen to such desolation in a single day? Those in charge are deeply deluded—are they not!
units.literal: Moreover holding fullness and fearing surfeit is itself the old wind of our house—why in one morning fall to such desolation? Those in charge are bitterly deluded—will it not be so!

units.zh: 詎容都不先聞，或可不知耳。
units.en: Could you not have told me first—or perhaps you did not know.
units.literal: How could it be tolerated that you did not inform me first—or perhaps you did not know.

units.zh: 衣冠胄胤，如吾者甚多，才能固不足道，唯不傾側溢詐，士頗以此容之。
units.en: There are many scions of great houses like me; my talent is nothing to speak of—only in not leaning and overflowing with deceit do gentlemen somewhat tolerate me.
units.literal: Capped and belted descendants like me are many; talent and ability are certainly not worth speaking of—only in not leaning and overflowing with deceit do gentlemen somewhat tolerate me for this.

units.zh: 至於規矩細行，難可詳料。
units.en: As for rules of conduct and small proprieties, these are hard to reckon in detail.
units.literal: As for rules and minute conduct, it is hard to reckon in detail.

units.zh: 疹疾日滋，縱恣益甚，人道所貴，廢不復脩。
units.en: My rash illness grows daily and my indulgence ever worse; what human conduct esteems I have abandoned and no longer cultivate.
units.literal: Rash illness daily increases, indulgence and license ever more severe; what human conduct esteems I abandon and no longer cultivate.

units.zh: 幸值聖明相容，置之教外，且舊恩所及，每蒙寬假。
units.en: Fortunately a sage ruler tolerates me and sets me outside ordinary discipline; where old favor reaches I always receive leniency.
units.literal: Fortunately meeting a sage and enlightened ruler who tolerates me, placing me outside instruction, and moreover where old favor reaches I always receive lenient indulgence.

units.zh: 吾亦自揆疾疹重侵，難復支振，民生安樂之事，心死久矣。
units.en: I also know that rash illness has heavily invaded me and I can hardly hold myself up; the pleasures of life have been dead to my heart for long.
units.literal: I also estimate for myself that rash illness heavily invades and I can hardly support myself again; the affairs of life's ease and joy—my heart has long been dead to them.

units.zh: 所以解日偷存，盡於大布糲粟，半夕安寢，便以自度，血氣盈虛，不復稍道，長以大散為和羹，弟為不見之邪？
units.en: Therefore I steal through my days on coarse cloth and plain grain; half a night's sleep is my measure of well-being; I no longer speak of the ebb and flow of my vitality; I have long taken powdered medicine as my sustenance—do you not see this, younger brother?
units.literal: Therefore I pass days stealing survival, exhausting coarse cloth and coarse grain; half a night's peaceful sleep I take as self-measurement; fullness and emptiness of blood and breath I no longer speak of slightly; long taking great powder as harmonizing broth—do you not see this, younger brother?

units.zh: 疾廢居然，且事一己，上不足敗俗傷化，下不至毀辱家門，泊爾尸居，無方待化。
units.en: Settled in illness and disability, serving only myself—I am not enough to ruin custom above or shame my family below; I dwell like a corpse, awaiting transformation without method.
units.literal: Illness and disability settled thus, and serving only oneself—above not enough to ruin custom and harm transformation, below not reaching to destroy and shame the family gate; placidly like a corpse dwelling, with no method awaiting transformation.

units.zh: 凡此二三，皆是事實。
units.en: All of this is fact.
units.literal: All these two or three are matters of fact.

units.zh: 吾與弟書，不得家中相欺也。
units.en: In writing to you, younger brother, we must not deceive each other within the family.
units.literal: In my letter to you, younger brother, one must not deceive each other within the family.

units.zh: 州陵此舉，為無所因，反覆思之，了不能解。
units.en: Zhouling's action has no cause I can see; thinking it over repeatedly I cannot understand it at all.
units.literal: Zhouling's action in this has no cause whatsoever; thinking it over repeatedly I utterly cannot understand.

units.zh: 豈見吾近者諸牋邪，良可怪笑。
units.en: Did he see my recent letters? That would be truly laughable.
units.literal: Did he see my recent various memorials? Truly something to marvel and laugh at.

units.zh: 吾少學作文，又晚節如小進，使君公欲民不偷，每加存飾，酬對尊貴，不厭敬恭。
units.en: From youth I studied composition, and in later years made some small progress; when lords wished the people not remiss, I always added polish; in answering the great I was never weary of respect.
units.literal: From youth I studied composing writing, and in late years made a small advance; the lord and gentleman wishing the people not to be remiss, each time added preservation and adornment; replying to the honored and noble, never weary of respect and reverence.

units.zh: 且文詞不怨思抑揚，則流澹無味。
units.en: Moreover if literary language lacks modulation of feeling, it flows thin and tasteless.
units.literal: Moreover if literary words lack grievance-thought and modulation, they flow thin and without flavor.

units.zh: 文好古，貴能連類可悲，一往視之，如似多意。
units.en: Writing favors antiquity and values the power to link images into pathos; read through at once it seems full of hidden meaning.
units.literal: Writing favors antiquity, esteeming ability to link categories into what is lamentable; reading through at once it seems to have much meaning.

units.zh: 當見居非求志，清論所排，便是通辭訴屈邪。
units.en: When one sees that one's position is not what one sought and pure discourse rejects it—is that then a general complaint of wrongs?
units.literal: When one sees that dwelling is not seeking one's aim, what pure discourse excludes—is that then general language lodging grievance?

units.zh: 爾者真可謂真素寡矣！
units.en: In that case one may truly be called lacking in plain authenticity!
units.literal: In that case one may truly be called poor in plain authenticity!

units.zh: 其數旦見客小防，自來盈門，亦不煩獨舉吉也。
units.en: I receive visitors only on a few guarded days; they come of themselves filling the gate—I need not trouble to raise auspicious words alone.
units.literal: The number of days I receive guests is small and guarded; they come of themselves filling the gate—I also do not trouble to raise auspicious words alone.

units.zh: 此輩乃云語勢所至，非其要也。
units.en: These people say it is only the momentum of language, not its essence.
units.literal: This crowd then says it is where the momentum of language arrives, not its essentials.

units.zh: 弟無懷居今地，萬物初不以相非，然魯器齊虛，實宜書紳。
units.en: Younger brother, do not be complacent in your present place; all things do not reject each other at first—yet the story of Lu's vessels and Qi's emptiness truly should be written on one's sash.
units.literal: Younger brother, do not harbor dwelling in this place; all things at first do not reject each other—yet Lu vessels and Qi emptiness truly should be written on the sash.

units.zh: 今三署六府之人，誰表裏此內，儻疑弟豫有力，於素論何如哉。
units.en: Among the men of the three offices and six ministries today, who knows the inside and outside of this—if they suspect you had foreknowledge and influence, what of plain discourse?
units.literal: Now among the men of the three offices and six ministries, who inside and outside this—if they suspect younger brother had foreknowledge and power, what of plain discourse?

units.zh: 則吾長阨不死，終誤盛壯也。
units.en: Then I will long linger in obstruction without dying, ultimately misleading my prime years.
units.literal: Then I will long be blocked and not die, ultimately misleading my prime and vigor.

units.zh: 江不過強吹拂吾，云是巖穴人。
units.en: Jiang merely pressed and flattered me, calling me a man of cliff and cave.
units.literal: Jiang merely forcibly blew and brushed me, saying I am a man of cliff and cave.

units.zh: 巖穴人情所高，吾得當此，則雞鶩變作鳳皇，何為干飾廉隅，秩秩見於面目，所惜者大耳。
units.en: Men of cliff and cave are what the world esteems; given this title, chickens and ducks become phoenixes—why bother adorning one's integrity, showing it orderly in one's face? What I regret is the greater matter only.
units.literal: Cliff-and-cave men are what human sentiment esteems; obtaining this, then chickens and ducks change into phoenixes—why bother adorning corner integrity, orderly appearing on the face? What is regretted is great only.

units.zh: 諸舍闔門皆蒙時私，此既未易陳道，故常因含聲不言。
units.en: All our households have received private favor of the time; this is not easy to state, so I often hold my tongue.
units.literal: All the households with closed gates received private favor of the time; this is already not easy to set forth, therefore I often hold sound within and do not speak.

units.zh: 至兄弟，尤為叨竊，臨海頻煩二郡，謙亦越進清階，吾高枕家巷，遂至中書郎，此足以闔棺矣。
units.en: As for my brothers, they have been especially presumptuous—Linhai repeatedly held two commanderies, Qian also rose beyond his station; I with high pillow in my lane reached Palace Gentleman—this is enough to close the coffin.
units.literal: As for brothers, especially presumptuous theft—Linhai repeatedly troubled two commanderies, Qian also overstepped into pure ranks; I with high pillow in the home lane reached Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat—this is enough to close the coffin.

units.zh: 又前年優旨，自弟所宣，雖夏后撫辜人，周宣及鰥寡，不足過也。
units.en: Moreover the favorable edict of two years ago was proclaimed by you; though Yu comforted the guilty and King Xuan of Zhou reached widows and orphans, they could not surpass it.
units.literal: Moreover the favorable edict of the year before last was proclaimed by you, younger brother; though Xia Hou comforted the guilty man and Zhou Xuan reached widowers and widows, it is not enough to surpass this.

units.zh: 語皆循檢校跡，不為虛飾也。
units.en: The words all follow verified facts and are not empty adornment.
units.literal: The words all follow inspected traces and are not empty adornment.

units.zh: 作人不阿諛，無緣頭髮見白，稍學諂詐。
units.en: By nature I do not flatter; without cause for my hair to turn white, I would slightly learn flattery and deceit.
units.literal: Making a man I do not flatter and fawn; without cause for hair to show white, slightly learning flattery and deceit.

units.zh: 且吾何以為，足不能行，自不得出戶；
units.en: Moreover what can I do—my feet cannot walk, so I naturally cannot leave the house;
units.literal: Moreover what can I do—feet cannot walk, naturally cannot go out the door;

units.zh: 頭不耐風，故不可扶曳。
units.en: my head cannot bear wind, so I cannot be supported and led along.
units.literal: the head cannot bear wind, therefore cannot be supported and dragged.

units.zh: 家本貧餧，至於惡衣蔬食，設使盜蹠居此，亦不能兩展其足，妄意珍藏也。
units.en: Our family was originally poor, to the point of coarse clothes and plain food; even Robber Zhi dwelling here could not stretch both feet twice, vainly dreaming of hoarded treasure.
units.literal: The family was originally poor and hungry, to the point of detestable clothes and vegetable food; suppose Robber Zhi dwelt here, he also could not stretch both feet twice, vainly intending treasured store.

units.zh: 正令選官設作此舉，於吾亦無劍戟之傷，所以懃懃畏人之多言也。
units.en: Even if the selection official made this appointment, it would not wound me like sword or halberd; what I earnestly fear is people's gossip.
units.literal: Even if the selection official set up this action, for me there is also no wound of sword and halberd; therefore I earnestly fear people's much talk.

units.zh: 管子晉賢，乃關人主之輕重，此何容易哉。
units.en: Guanzi was a worthy man of Jin, yet concerned the ruler's weight in the balance—how is this easy!
units.literal: Guanzi was Jin's worthy man, yet concerned the ruler's light and heavy—how is this easy!

units.zh: 州陵亦自言視明聽聰，而返區區飾吾，何辯致而下英俊。
units.en: Zhouling also claims clear sight and keen hearing, yet turns to petty flattery of me—what eloquence can bring down outstanding men?
units.literal: Zhouling also himself says he sees clearly and hears keenly, yet returns to petty adorning me—what eloquence to bring down outstanding men.

units.zh: 夫奇士必龍居深藏，與蛙蝦為伍，放勳其猶難之，林宗輩不足識也。
